analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_sfifo_wr.sv:158 `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & reg_full;`. The block term w_wr_blk (line 114: `reg_sw_rst_busy | ~i_rst_n_sw`) is left out, even though the comment on line 157 says "A blocked write ... raises no pulse". Line 234 drives o_overflow from reg_overflow. reg_full (line 155, `w_occ_nxt >= PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH`) keeps updating while the software reset blocks writes. So any edge with i_wr_en=1 and reg_full=1 during a block gives o_overflow=1. The read side has the block term: rtl/m_vlsit_sfifo_rd.sv:154 `reg_underflow <= i_rd_en & ~w_rd_blk & reg_empty;`. Inference for the failing edge: the RTL gives 1 only when i_wr_en=1 and reg_full=1, and that makes o_full=1 (line 232). The monitor expected 0, so P.sw==0 or P.busy==1 must have held. The failing edge was therefore a software-reset-blocked write. sim.log:48 records only the assertion message, not the pre-edge port values.
analyses.test_does: test_chk_013 (test_sync_fifo.py:718-735) runs Env.start((10,10)), then hw_reset for each release order, then random_traffic with sw_prob=0.02 (line 730). _rand_writer (lines 515-542) drives i_rst_n_sw=0 for 1..10 cycles at random. It keeps driving i_wr_en at random density (line 541) while the reset is low and while busy, so blocked writes happen. The passive Monitor checks at every i_clk_wr rise with i_rst_n_wr=1 (line 217). In _wr_edge (lines 303-306) it computes exp_ovf = we AND P.full==1 AND P.sw==1 AND P.busy==0 from the pre-edge port snapshot and asserts S.ovf == exp_ovf. The expected value follows CHK-011 / REQ-FUNC-008 / REQ-SRST-002 directly. The SVA verif/sva/nnc_chk_wr.sv:88 uses the same equation.

candidates.evidence_for: m_vlsit_sfifo_wr.sv:158 does not include ~w_wr_blk. That contradicts spec:536 ("i_wr_en AND NOT block AND full flop"), spec:150 and spec:288, and the RTL's own comment at line 157. The read-side twin (m_vlsit_sfifo_rd.sv:154) does include ~w_rd_blk. Given line 158, a mismatch with exp=0/got=1 can only happen on a blocked write, which is exactly the excluded case. The same failure appears in every ratio of CHK-013 and in all software-reset tests (CHK-022, CHK-024), while tests without a software reset (CHK-015, CHK-016, CHK-019, CHK-020) pass with correct overflow pulses (sim.log:278-295).
